sections.title: MCP first, the CLI by exception
sections.lead: An agent reaches Orbit through Orbit's MCP tools whenever its tool list has them: they are checked against their schema, need no shell, and carry this session's identity without an argument.
points: Claude Code lists them as mcp__orbit__<tool>; Codex and the other engines show the same server's tools under their own prefix.
Every write answers with a receipt: ok, outcome, the entity's id and its status. A write happened only when the receipt says ok: true and outcome: written.
When the agent is unsure which tool fits or how to call it, it calls guide: with no arguments for the routes, with a topic for the recipe. guide is listed in every session, whatever its switches.
MCP and the CLI reach the same server with the same approvals, attribution and ids: a task created on one is read on the other with no translation.
asks: Which Orbit tools do you have in this session?
Call guide and tell me which tool records a follow-up.

sections.title: Your record and the agent's private plan
sections.lead: Orbit is your durable record; the engine's own todo or plan tool is the agent's private scratch.
points: A plan the engine keeps lives in this conversation only: nobody else sees it, and a compaction can drop it.
Work you want kept or followed up goes to Orbit, where it has an id and a status that you, the apps and later sessions can read.
The agent never calls a private plan a task, and never says it filed something without an id Orbit returned.
When you say "keep that plan", the plan becomes one task_create_batch: one task per item, its order as dependsOnRefs, its parts as parentRef, in one call and one card.
asks: Think this migration through first; don't file anything yet.
OK, keep that plan in Orbit.

sections.title: Which object a request belongs to
sections.lead: Each request goes to the object that answers its question; when two fit, the smaller one wins.
points: Project: What is the whole thing for, and what settles it?
Task: What is the one piece of work?
Task list: How is this class of work dispatched?
Session: What is running right now?
Agent: Where does it run, and under which identity?
Not every request is an Orbit write: answering a question, explaining or editing code records nothing.
asks: Remember to rotate the staging key.
What is still open in the agent-contract project?

sections.title: Creating is not starting
sections.lead: task_create records work and runs nothing in the call; starting it is a decision of its own.
points: task_start runs work that is already recorded, on its assignee, once its prerequisites are DONE.
task_create with startNow: true records the work and starts it on one card.
runAt starts it once, at a set time; it is not a deadline (that is dueDate).
autoRunWhenReady defaults to true: an assigned task in a started project starts by itself once every prerequisite is DONE. To hold work until you say so, the agent passes autoRunWhenReady: false.
Your own "Create and start" on the card starts it even if the agent asked for no start, and the agent does not undo that.
asks: File this for later; nobody should start it until I say so.
Run the recorded migration task now.

sections.title: When the CLI is the right tool
sections.lead: The Orbit CLI is for what MCP does not do well: pipes and scripts, bulk input from a file or stdin, the few operations with no MCP tool, and commands that must outlive the turn.
points: The agent runs it by the absolute path Orbit gives it, never an orbit found on PATH: a project-local binary is not this runner's CLI.
It finds a command with orbit guide [topic] --json or orbit capabilities --id <id> --json, and runs the argv they return.
--receipt prints the same receipt the MCP tool answers with, and the command exits 0 exactly when it wrote; --json prints the entity alone.
Never to get around a card, a refusal or a switch: the CLI reaches the same server under the same approvals, so a declined card or a missing switch there is the same answer.
Outside a session, a script files work as you, with a personal access token (ORBIT_USER_TOKEN): the runner's own credential has no card-free door.
The operations with no MCP tool are session_import, wiki_import, wiki_verify; the agent runs them at the CLI.
asks: File the 30 issues in issues.csv as tasks.
Give me a command I can put in cron that files tomorrow's checklist.

sections.title: When something is missing
sections.lead: Every refusal says why and what to do, and none of them is solved by another door: the switches stay where they are, and Agent tools shows which one is off.
points: Agent tools on the session shows whether its engine started Orbit's MCP server, and in the engine's own words why not.
A missing family of tools is a switch: Session orchestration for sessions, agents and runners; Watch for waits; the wiki for the wiki.
A refused call answers with a receipt whose error.code and error.retry say what to do; the table below reads them for you.
asks: Why can't you start a session for this?
Call guide and tell me which Orbit tools you have and why any are missing.

routes.intent: Remember this, file it, do it later, someone should fix it
Keep this plan: it is already worked out and counted
Set up this whole body of work, with its own goal and acceptance (4+ dependent steps, or several agents over days)
Run it now; it is already recorded
Run it now; it is not recorded yet
Do it at a set time
Hand this to another agent as its own conversation
What is the state of this project, task or session?
Remember this lesson or pitfall about a file or a pattern
Keep this file, or read one back
This class of work needs its own dispatch policy
Which agent should run this, or change an agent's defaults

rules: R2: The smaller object wins: one task beats a project; one task beats a batch of one.
R3: Never double-record: not a task per step of the current task, not a task for the current task, not a session to do what this turn can do.
R4: Read before write when the destination is uncertain: task_list --project-id, project_get, or task_create_batch dryRun.
R5: An engine plan/todo is private scratch; never call it an Orbit record, never claim a task without its id, never refuse to record work because a private plan covers it.

troubleshooting.symptom: The agent has no Orbit tools.
troubleshooting.cause: Its engine did not start Orbit's MCP server. Agent tools on the session shows Not connected, with the engine's own reason.
troubleshooting.fix: The agent can still use the Orbit CLI by the absolute path in its instructions, under the same approvals. A new session starts the server again.

troubleshooting.symptom: No session, agent or runner tools, and a hand-off is filed as a task.
troubleshooting.cause: Session orchestration is off for this account.
troubleshooting.fix: Turn it on in Settings → Session orchestration. A session started before that gets the tools when its engine next starts; turning it off takes effect at once.

troubleshooting.symptom: No task_await, session_await or watch tools.
troubleshooting.cause: Watch is off for this account on this Orbit server.
troubleshooting.fix: Nothing to change in the session: the agent looks again in a later turn instead of waiting.

troubleshooting.cause: The wiki is off for this account on this Orbit server.
troubleshooting.fix: The agent works from the code and from what you tell it.

troubleshooting.symptom: A write is refused with SESSION_IN_PLAN_MODE.
troubleshooting.cause: The session is in Plan: Orbit's reads, waits and questions for you run, and every other write waits for the plan's approval.
troubleshooting.fix: Approve the plan or change the session's permission mode; the agent makes the write then.

troubleshooting.symptom: A write is refused with PERMISSION_MODE_UNREADABLE.
troubleshooting.cause: The session's process could not read its permission mode from the runner, so it wrote nothing.
troubleshooting.fix: The same call is safe to send again. If it keeps happening, the runner restarted under the session: start a new one.

troubleshooting.symptom: The agent says you declined a card.
troubleshooting.cause: You answered the card with no.
troubleshooting.fix: Nothing was written, and the agent does not create it another way. Ask again in your own words if you change your mind.

troubleshooting.cause: Its card is waiting for your answer; the runner holds the call meanwhile.
troubleshooting.fix: Answer the card in the app; the agent is woken with your answer. A card that waits is not a no.

troubleshooting.symptom: The agent replies to what you wrote on a card instead of filing.
troubleshooting.cause: You pressed Chat about this: that is a conversation, not a no, and nothing was written.
troubleshooting.fix: Once you agree, the agent calls again, changed as agreed, and you get a new card.

troubleshooting.symptom: A call is refused with INVALID_ARGUMENTS.
troubleshooting.cause: Its arguments do not fit the tool's schema; the receipt names every field that does not.
troubleshooting.fix: The agent fixes the fields it names and calls again: nothing was sent.

troubleshooting.symptom: A create comes back with outcome unknown.
troubleshooting.cause: It was sent and no answer came back, so it may have landed.
troubleshooting.fix: The agent reads first (task_list) and only then decides; a create keyed with idempotencyKey is resent by the runner under the same key and cannot file twice.

troubleshooting.symptom: A script on the runner is refused with TASK_WRITE_NEEDS_OWNER_CARD.
troubleshooting.cause: Outside a session, the runner's own credential cannot file work: that would be a way around your cards.
troubleshooting.fix: Run the script with your personal access token (ORBIT_USER_TOKEN); the work is recorded as you.

troubleshooting.symptom: An orbit command behaves unlike the agent's tools.
troubleshooting.cause: A different orbit was found on PATH, such as a project-local build.
troubleshooting.fix: The agent runs the absolute path in its instructions; capabilities --json names the cliVersion that answered.

examples.title: File many tasks from a script
examples.ask: File the 30 issues in issues.txt as tasks, held until I start them.
examples.does: Uses the CLI's bulk door instead of one task_create per line: a script turns the file into one --tasks document (at most 50 items), a dry run shows where it lands, and one create-batch writes it on one card.
examples.script:
jq -R -s 'split("\n") | map(select(length > 0)) | {tasks: map({title: ., description: ("Fix: " + .), completionCriterion: "EVIDENCE_JUDGMENT", acceptanceCriteria: "<what settles it>", autoRunWhenReady: false})}' issues.txt > plan.json
orbit task create-batch --tasks-file - --dry-run --json < plan.json
orbit task create-batch --tasks-file - --idempotency-key issues-txt-part-1 --receipt < plan.json
examples.proof: --receipt prints one receipt with every item's id in input order, and the command exits 0 exactly when it wrote. Outside a session the same command runs with ORBIT_USER_TOKEN and is recorded as you.

playbooks.title: Keep a worked-out plan
playbooks.when: The person asks you to keep a plan that is already worked out and counted, or several related pieces of work at once.
steps: Pick the record. One item is one task_create. Several related items are one task_create_batch (at most 50). A body of work with its own goal and acceptance, 4 or more dependent steps or several agents over days, may be proposed as project_create first; its card is the person's answer, and a no means tasks.
Give every item a ref (s1, s2, ...). Order with dependsOnRefs (when an item may run) and nest with parentRef (what it is part of). dependsOnTaskIds and parentTaskId name tasks that already exist.
Ask the person what would settle each item and pass their words as acceptanceCriteria; declare completionCriterion on every item. If they have not said, ask and end your turn.
Hold what must not start: autoRunWhenReady: false on that item. startNow: true only on an item they want running now.
Unsure where it lands? Call task_create_batch with dryRun: true first: it writes nothing and asks nobody.
Say in a sentence or two what you are about to file, then call task_create_batch once, keyed with an idempotencyKey derived from the plan.
Read the receipt: ok: true, outcome: written, items[] in input order, each with its id. Link each as [title](orbit-task:<id>). A declined card is a refusal: do not file it another way.

playbooks.title: File many tasks from a file
playbooks.when: The work arrives as a file or a list too long to type: issues in a text file or a CSV, lines of a checklist.
steps: Use the CLI's bulk door, by the absolute path your instructions give, never one task_create per line.
Build one --tasks document of at most 50 items with a script; every item carries title, description, completionCriterion and acceptanceCriteria, and autoRunWhenReady: false when it must wait.
Preview it: orbit task create-batch --tasks-file - --dry-run --json writes nothing and says where every item would land.
Write it: orbit task create-batch --tasks-file - --idempotency-key <a slug of the batch> --receipt. Inside a session it puts one card in front of the person; it exits 0 exactly when it wrote.
More than 50 items: split them into parts, each with its own key. A part that fails can be sent again with the same key and cannot file twice.

Outside a session (cron, CI) run the same command with the person's own token: ORBIT_USER_TOKEN=<token> orbit task create-batch ... is recorded as them and needs no card. The runner's machine credential cannot file work on its own (TASK_WRITE_NEEDS_OWNER_CARD).
playbooks.code:
jq -R -s 'split("\n") | map(select(length > 0)) | {tasks: map({title: ., description: ("Fix: " + .), completionCriterion: "EVIDENCE_JUDGMENT", acceptanceCriteria: "<what settles it>", autoRunWhenReady: false})}' issues.txt > plan.json
orbit task create-batch --tasks-file - --dry-run --json < plan.json
orbit task create-batch --tasks-file - --idempotency-key issues-txt-part-1 --receipt < plan.json

playbooks.title: Hand work off now
playbooks.when: The person wants work running now, by another agent or in a conversation of its own.
steps: Recorded already, with every prerequisite DONE: task_start on it. Its receipt names the started session.
Not recorded yet: task_create with startNow: true. One card covers the create and the start; do not call task_start after it.

The person wants a separate conversation rather than a work item: session_create on an agent. It exists only with Session orchestration on, and a sub-session never gets a wider permission mode than yours.
No session_* tools in your list: orchestration is off. Record the work as a task, tell the person the switch is in Settings -> Session orchestration, and never claim a delegation.
Then wait without polling: task_await or session_await, and end your turn. Orbit starts a new turn in this session when it finishes.

playbooks.title: Find out why an Orbit tool is missing or refused
playbooks.when: A tool you expected is not in your list, or a call was refused and you are not sure why.
steps: Call guide: it is listed in every session and only reads. Its index says, route by route, whether the route is available here and why not.

No Orbit tools at all: your engine did not start Orbit's MCP server. Use the CLI at the absolute path your instructions give: orbit guide --json, then orbit capabilities --summary --json, whose unavailable and withheld groups say why each command is missing.
A refused call: read its receipt, not its prose. error.code says what happened and error.retry what to do: resend, reread_first, fix_input, do_not_retry or wait.
Never get around a refusal by changing surfaces: MCP and the CLI reach the same server under the same approvals, so the answer would be the same, and a second ask without a new question.
Tell the person what is missing and where the switch is; the switches are theirs to change.

instructionsNote: Orbit's own instructions are the same words on every engine: they begin with the primer, and nothing in a repository, a CLAUDE.md or an AGENTS.md, adds to them or takes them away. Where they disagree with your own message, your message steers the turn.

permissionModes.label: Plan
permissionModes.orbit: Orbit's reads, waits and questions for you run. Every other Orbit write is refused with SESSION_IN_PLAN_MODE until the plan is approved, and background jobs are refused.

permissionModes.label: Default
permissionModes.orbit: Orbit's reads and waits run unasked. A create, a batch, a project, a provider or an agent change puts a card in front of you first, and a background job asks before it starts.

permissionModes.label: Accept Edits
permissionModes.orbit: As Default for Orbit's calls: a create, a batch or a project still puts a card in front of you, and a background job asks before it starts.

permissionModes.label: Don't Ask
permissionModes.orbit: Orbit's reads and writes run unasked, except a write that needs your card, which still asks. Background jobs are refused.

permissionModes.label: Auto
permissionModes.orbit: Orbit's calls run, and a write that needs your card still asks; on Codex a destructive call goes to Codex's own review first. Background jobs start without asking.

permissionModes.label: Bypass
permissionModes.orbit: Orbit's calls run, and a write that needs your card still asks. Background jobs start without asking.

orchestration.on: Session orchestration is on for this account: the agent may open and steer sessions, and manage this account's agents and runners. A sub-session never gets a wider permission mode than this one.
orchestration.off: Session orchestration is off for this account, so the agent has no session, agent or runner tools and records a hand-off as a task instead. Turn it on in Settings → Session orchestration.

status.connected: {engine} started Orbit's MCP server and lists {tools} Orbit tools.
status.failed: {engine} could not start Orbit's MCP server.
status.fallback: Orbit's runtime instructions still reached the agent, so it can use the Orbit CLI by its absolute path, under the same approvals. A new session starts the server again.
status.needs_auth: {engine} is waiting for a sign-in before it starts Orbit's MCP server.
status.not_configured: {engine} was started without Orbit's MCP server.
status.not_reported: This session's engine does not report its MCP connections to the runner.
status.starting: {engine} is still starting Orbit's MCP server.

skill.purpose: Orbit's long recipes: keeping a worked-out plan as one batch, filing many tasks from a file with the CLI, handing work off now, and finding out why an Orbit tool is missing or refused. Optional: guide and the tools' own descriptions are enough for any single call.

switchReasons.not_connected: The MCP server is not connected.
switchReasons.orchestration: Session orchestration is off for this account.
switchReasons.watches: Watch is off for this account on this Orbit server.
switchReasons.wiki: The wiki is off for this account on this Orbit server.
